* The petitioner no.1, Rajkumari, was arrested by the police in connection with a strike by workers in the Noida Industrial Area, Faridabad and Delhi on 11.8.1997.
* The petitioner no.1 alleged that she was arrested at around 1.30 a.m. in the night intervening 15/16.8.1997, without being informed of the grounds of her arrest and without being given the opportunity to meet her lawyer during interrogation.
* The respondents, however, denied these allegations and stated that the petitioner no.1 was arrested at around 5.30 a.m. on 16.8.1997, after the grounds of her arrest were explained to her and after she was given the opportunity to meet her lawyer during interrogation.

Issues:

* Whether the petitioner no.1 was arrested in violation of her fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 21 and 22(1) of the Constitution of India.
* Whether the respondents complied with the provisions of Section 50 of the Cr.P.C. and the safeguards contained in the DO letter dated 10/14.3.1980 of the Home Secretary, Government of India.

Statute:

* The Cr.P.C.
* The Constitution of India

Ruling by Present Court (Decision):

* The Court held that the petitioner no.1 was not arrested in violation of her fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 21 and 22(1) of the Constitution of India.
* The Court further held that the respondents complied with the provisions of Section 50 of the Cr.P.C. and the safeguards contained in the DO letter dated 10/14.3.1980 of the Home Secretary, Government of India.
* The Court also held that there was no need to issue any general direction to the respondents to stop arresting women between sunset and sunrise except in grave offences like murder.

Conclusion:

* The Court dismissed the writ petitions and the contempt petitions, holding that the petitioner no.1 was not arrested in violation of her fundamental rights and that the respondents complied with the relevant provisions of law.
